To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The recoil proton polarizations in the p({r vec e},e{prime} {r vec p}) reaction were measured for the first time.

we have measured the recoil proton polarization observables D{sup scr(l)} and D{sup scr(t)} for the p(e,e{prime}p) and d(e,e{prime})n reactions, and the induced neutron polarization, P{sub n}, for the d(e,e{primes}p)n reaction, under identical kinematics, and that our results are in good accord with the plane wave impulse approximation.
1) The deuteron and proton polarization observables agree with PWIA calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spin structure of the nucleon, specifically, the proton and neutron.

the study of the structure and dynamics of the nucleon using electron scattering from hydrogen and deuterated targets at Q{sup 1} = 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8 GeV{sup 2}. The primary focus of our research is the determination of the proton and deuteron spin structure functions and the measurement of the proton recoil polarization in the p(e, e{prime} p) reaction.
the measurement of the polarization observables in the p({r vec e},e{r vec p}) reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PWIA describes the spin observables for both the p and d reactions, but the agreement between the data and PWIA is not as good as for the unpolarized observables.
, for the first time, the polarization observables in electron scattering from hydrogen and deuterons were measured under identical experimental conditions.
, in general, the PWIA describes the data well.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deuteron data provide the first direct evidence for final-state interactions in the deuteron.
our results are in good general agreement with the PWIA and with the predictions of our theoretical model.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to measure recoil proton polarizations in the quasi-elastic region of both hydrogen and deuterated targets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the deuteron is a good approximation of the proton.

the polarization observables are very sensitive to the underlying nuclear dynamics.
